bull_case: Qualification, reliability, localization and UHV capability deepen switching costs.
bear_case: Little software-like network/data feedback exists; industry capacity expansion can erode scarcity rents.
thesis: The moat is industrial—qualification, reliability, engineering, delivery and localization—not a classic data/network ecosystem.

evidence.claim: U.S./Korean capacity is expanding alongside UHV orders.
H1 R&D was ₩49.3bn across power equipment, ICT and systems.

counterevidence: No compounding software/data network effect is demonstrated.
Peers can add local transformer capacity.
falsifiers: If competitor capacity cuts price/margin while customers switch without qualification friction, the moat is weakening.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Backlog, repeat utility demand, utilization and margin do not show persistent moat contraction.

key_kpis.name: gross margin + qualification wins
key_kpis.threshold: stable margins and repeat UHV awards

subscores.rationale: Repeat utility revenue, multi-year backlog and ~25% margin support switching/pricing; capacity expansion is the strongest counter.
Strict observable table: some scale/qualification evidence exists, but not 3+ same-definition ecosystem metrics with network/data trend and switching cost.
UHV engineering, certification, delivery and localization are multiple defense layers; industry supply remains a risk.

uncertainties.rationale: Scarcity and switching costs are hard to separate.
This criterion fits industrial equipment poorly and numeric ecosystem evidence is limited.
